h: Making a Seaside Day of It
p: Bournemouth does seaside days brilliantly, and the Oceanarium slots right into the middle of one. A good plan is to check the forecast and use it to shape the day. Bright morning? Get on the beach early, then duck inside when the sun gets too strong or the clouds roll in. Grey all day? Make the Oceanarium the main event and head out for a brisk walk along the prom afterwards. The visit doesn't take all day, so you've got plenty of flexibility either side.

Inside, give yourself time at each zone and catch any talks or feeding sessions that appeal, as they're where the kids tend to learn the most. Booking ahead is wise in the busy summer season and during school holidays, when the seafront gets packed.

Once you're back outside, there's no shortage of ways to fill the rest of the day. The Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum, perched on the East Cliff, is a wonderfully over-the-top Victorian villa full of treasures, with sea views from its gardens. Boscombe, a short walk or bus ride east, has its own pier and a more laid-back feel. Further on, Hengistbury Head offers heathland walks, views across Christchurch Harbour and the colourful beach huts on Mudeford Sandbank. Heading west, Sandbanks and Poole Harbour have sweeping sands and water sports, and Poole Quay is a lively spot for an evening stroll and some fish and chips by the boats.
